subject: nose-horned viper
title: A Viper Swallowed a Centipede. The Centipede Ate Its Way Back Out

scenes.text: A snake swallowed a centipede. The centipede won.
Golem Grad, an island in Lake Prespa, North Macedonia, 2013. A young nose-horned viper, 20 centimeters long, found dead under a stone.
Its belly was torn open. Sticking out of it: the head of a 15 centimeter centipede, Scolopendra. Also dead.
The centipede weighed 4.8 grams. The snake, 4.2. It had swallowed something heavier than itself, alive.
When scientists opened the viper, its organs were gone. The whole body was filled by the centipede, which had chewed its way out from inside.
Both died. But only one of them was the meal.

description:
A young viper swallowed a centipede heavier than itself. The centipede ate its way out.
On Golem Grad island in North Macedonia, researchers found a 20 cm nose-horned viper dead under a stone with the head of a 15 cm Scolopendra centipede protruding from its ruptured belly. The centipede weighed 4.8 grams, 114 percent of the snake's 4.2 grams. Dissection showed the snake's internal organs were missing; its body was filled by the centipede, which had apparently damaged the digestive organs from inside before both animals died. The case was published in Ecologica Montenegrina in 2014.
Which animal has bitten off more than it could chew in your opinion?
first_comment: The snake was a juvenile; young vipers on this island are known to eat centipedes. Which predator do you think picks the most dangerous prey?
